lessons.lesson: L1 Reading & Analysing an Unseen Poem

findings.claim: "Question 27 asks you to analyse a single unseen poem and is worth 24 marks. Question 28 asks you to compare the first poem with a second unseen poem and is worth 8 marks... 25 minutes on Q27 and 20 minutes on Q28."
findings.verdict: WRONG. AQA 8702/2 has no Question 28. Section C is Question 27, split into 27.1 (24 marks) and 27.2 (8 marks). Confirmed on the specimen question paper (sub-part labels 27.1 / 27.2), the specimen mark scheme, and the live June 2023 and June 2024 mark schemes.
findings.action: FIXED - all Q27 -> Q27.1 and Q28 -> Q27.2 across content_html (n3), exam_tip_html (n26), knowledge_checks (2), flashcard_questions (4). 11 references corrected.

findings.claim: 24-mark band ladder: Top band (22-24) / Upper band (18-21) / Top band (13-17) / Upper-mid band (9-12) / Lower-mid band (5-8) / Lower band (1-4)
findings.verdict: WRONG on two counts. (a) Three of the six boundaries do not match AQA: the official ladder is Level 6 = 21-24, Level 5 = 17-20, Level 4 = 13-16, Level 3 = 9-12, Level 2 = 5-8, Level 1 = 1-4. (b) The label 'Top band' appears twice, so a student reading it sees the top band claim both 22-24 and 13-17.
findings.action: FIXED - boundaries corrected to AQA values; labels made six-distinct using the clean house ladder already used in the An Inspector Calls unit (Top / Upper / Upper-mid / Mid / Lower-mid / Lower). Descriptor prose left exactly as authored.

flagged.claim: exam_tip_html (n26): "Always refer to the poet as 'the poet' - not 'the author' or 'the writer.'"
flagged.analysis: Contradicted by AQA's own terminology. The spec's AO2 reads 'analyse the language, form and structure used by a WRITER', and every Section C mark-scheme descriptor says 'writer's methods' / 'writers' methods'. No mark is lost for saying 'writer'. The advice is defensible as a style preference (poet is more precise for a poem) but is stated as a rule, and a student who follows it will find the mark scheme itself breaking that rule. Left unedited because it is teaching advice, not a fact.
flagged.recommendation: Soften to a preference, e.g. 'poet' is the most precise term; 'writer' is also used by the mark scheme.

flagged.claim: Timing advice: 25 minutes on Q27.1 (24 marks) and 20 minutes on Q27.2 (8 marks).
flagged.analysis: Internally tense with L4, which tells students the comparison is worth a third as much and warns 'Don't spend more time on the comparison than on the main unseen question' (KC4 pairs 'Spending 30+ minutes' with 'Takes time from Q27.1 (worth 3x more)'). Giving an 8-mark task 44% of Section C time contradicts the 3:1 mark ratio the same unit teaches. AQA prescribes no timings, so this is a judgement call, not an error.
flagged.recommendation: Orchestrator to decide a house split; common teacher guidance is roughly 30-35 min on 27.1 and 10-15 min on 27.2.

findings.action: FIXED - boundaries corrected to 21-24 / 17-20 / 13-16 / 9-12 / 5-8 / 1-4; duplicate label removed.

flagged.claim: practice_questions[3] model answer: "Sibilance in 'she/corridors' creates a hushing quality."
flagged.analysis: Technically defensible - /S/ in 'she' and final /z/ in 'corridors' are both sibilants - but weak as a teaching example: the two sounds are different, the 'corridors' sibilant is word-final and unstressed, and a student copying this pattern would be feature-spotting on thin evidence. The line's stronger sound feature is the plosive/fricative texture of 'crept... breath... ghost... cold'. A teacher could defend either reading.
flagged.recommendation: Consider replacing with a cleaner sibilance example, or reframing as assonance/consonance.

flagged.analysis: Cosmetic number disagreement, mirrored by 'themes', 'refrains', 'motifs', 'connotations', 'end-stopped lines' in this unit. The <dfn> tags wrap the inflected form as it appears in prose, so the glossary key follows the prose. Consistent across the whole subject, so not a unit-level defect.

flagged.claim: glossary_terms[0] has term '8 marks' with definition 'The marks available for Q27.2 (unseen poetry comparison) in AQA English Literature Paper 2 Section C. These 8 marks are assessed across AO2 only - analysis of methods.'
flagged.analysis: Orphan entry: a mark value is being used as a glossary term, and there is no matching <dfn class="term"> anywhere in the lesson, so it can never fire as a tooltip. cross_cutting_flags.scope: PLATFORM-WIDE - outside this unit, reported for the orchestrator
cross_cutting_flags.claim: scripts/lib/narration.py get_mp3_duration() returns wrong durations for every narration clip on the platform.
cross_cutting_flags.analysis: The function only accepts MPEG version 3 (MPEG-1) frame headers and uses BITRATES_V1 with SAMPLES_PER_FRAME = 1152. But the house narration format is 96 kbps 24 kHz mono, and 24 kHz is MPEG-2 Layer III, which uses 576 samples per frame and a different bitrate table. Measured with ffprobe on the 5 clips regenerated here: true 24.000 / 22.152 / 27.000 / 27.648 / 12.216 s against the library's 7.02 / 6.45 / 26.81 / 8.21 / 17.86 s. Errors reach 3.4x. This is the concrete cause behind the known 'narration manifest durations unreliable' note.
cross_cutting_flags.action: Corrected the 5 manifest durations touched by this batch to ffprobe-measured values, so nothing was left worse. The library bug and any platform-wide manifest re-measure are NOT in this unit's scope.
cross_cutting_flags.recommendation: Fix get_mp3_duration to handle MPEG-2/2.5 Layer III (576 samples per frame, V2 bitrate table), then re-measure manifests platform-wide from R2 without re-synthesising audio.
